items.excerpt: Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe Diyar Guldogan 12 November 2026• Update: 12 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Thursday, including US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arriving in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Israeli security cabinet ordering military to preparing for possible attack on Iran, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan highlighting importance of cleaner and more sustainable world for future generations during COP31. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Russian media reported. Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev met the two American representatives at Vnukovo Airport, Russian news agency Interfax reported. Russia's state-run TASS news agency also confirmed that the convoy carrying Dmitriev, Witkoff, and Kushner left the airport following their landing in the Russian capital. Kushner said Wednesday he and Witkoff will travel to Moscow following US-mediated trilateral peace negotiations with Russian and Ukrainian delegations. “One of the positives is we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, and we’re going to finalize the numbers tomorrow,” Kushner said. - Israeli security cabinet orders military to prepare for possible attack on Iran: Report Israel’s security cabinet has instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported Wednesday evening. “The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” the broadcaster said. KAN said the directives were made public after Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot issued a statement urging caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from unnecessary military operations until the next government is formed. The security cabinet last met on Oct. 5 – weeks before the Oct. 27 Israeli elections – the broadcaster added. - Turkish president urges cleaner, greener, fairer world for future generations Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan highlighted on Wednesday the importance of leaving a cleaner and more sustainable world for future generations during COP31, the UN Climate Change Conference in Türkiye. "The most precious legacy we can leave to future generations, before the world becomes uninhabitable, will be a cleaner, greener and fairer world," Erdogan said in a social media post. items.title: Treasury yields rise as investors await inflation and housing data
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Nov 12 2026 2:38 AM EST Hugh Leask U.S. Treasury yields edged higher Thursday as bond trading resumed after the Veterans Day closure and investors looked ahead to fresh inflation and housing data for clues about the economy and the Federal Reserve's next move. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury Add To Watchlist note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was up 2 basis points at 5.0100%. The 2-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist yield, which is more sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was 5 basis points higher at 4.7800%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist yield — which often moves on geopolitical developments — was steady at 5.3503%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another. The rise in yields comes as traders await more domestic data releases this week for fresh insights into the U.S. economic picture. On Friday, the latest monthly producer price inflation print, which tracks wholesale inflation, is expected to show a 0.4% rise in October, down from the 1.3% surge in September. Before that, investors are also looking out for October's home sales report from the National Association of Realtors, due later Thursday. Existing home sales rose by 1.5% in September to 3.99 million, up from a two-year low the previous month, and are expected to reach 4 million last month, according to Trading Economics estimates. Oil prices were broadly flat in early trading, as Middle East negotiations remain deadlocked. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures Add To Watchlist were up less than 0.1% at $86.59 a barrel, while Brent crude Add To Watchlist rose 0.17% to $92.92.

items.title: U.S. attorney demands Sen. Richard Blumenthal preserve documents from his inquiry into White House ballroom
items.excerpt: Nov. 11, 2026, 9:11 PM EST By Raquel Coronell Uribe, Ryan J. Reilly and Frank Thorp V A Justice Department official called on Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., on Wednesday to preserve documents related to what he claims is harassment of citizens during Blumenthal’s investigation into White House ballroom donors, threatening “significant legal consequences” if he does not comply. The U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, Aaron Reitz, alleged in a letter to Blumenthal that his investigation equated to threatening “citizens for associating themselves with the President and other public officials.” The White House warned congressional Democrats on Wednesday that efforts to investigate the administration could be a crime. In a post on X with a copy of the letter attached, Reitz equated Blumenthal’s investigation examining anonymous donors for the roughly $400 million project on White House grounds with wielding Congress as a “weapon” against Americans. “I’m taking the first step to stop this abuse of power,” Reitz said. Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, the second-highest-ranking official at the Justice Department, responded to Reitz’s post, saying, “The First Amendment expressly prohibits Congress from infringing the speech and association rights of Americans.” “DOJ will defend against threats to those rights, period,” McCotter wrote. Blumenthal said in a statement responding to the letter that he “will not be intimidated,” vowing to “vigorously pursue investigations into this Administration’s persistent misuse of taxpayer dollars and any corporate entity that has enabled their boundless corruption.” “The Trump Administration is so afraid of transparency and oversight that they are weaponizing the Department of Justice to baselessly target Congress in direct violation of the Constitution,” Blumenthal wrote. Blumenthal is the top Democrat on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. The subcommittee is tasked with studying the economics and efficiency of government operations. Blumenthal sent letters last month to a list of people whom a Washington Post report identified as having donated private funds to the ballroom’s construction. A news release said he was “leading an inquiry into waste, fraud, and abuse associated with the White House ballroom and other projects throughout the nation’s capital.” President Donald Trump had vowed to release the names of the private donors, but he has made only a partial list public. A few donors have acknowledged their donations, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who is under investigation by the company and the FBI for an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Trump defended Huang in remarks to reporters this week. Reitz’s letter cited the federal conspiracy against rights statute, as well as the federal deprivation of rights under color of law statute. Such an overt investigative measure against a sitting member of Congress would typically have undergone an extensive review process within the Justice Department’s Public Integrity Office, but that office has been shrunk and sidelined in the second Trump term. A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that “the Department routinely requests that records be preserved when public officials take such extreme actions,” alleging that Blumenthal’s letters were an attempt to “suppress their First Amendment activities, including their philanthropic practices.”

Colom noted Mississippi's civil rights history in his Wednesday night victory speech but pledged to represent all Mississippians. The Associated Press called the contest Wednesday evening. Hyde-Smith posted a concession video on social media. National and Mississippi Democrats are celebrating the win as a seismic shift in the state and region. Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews cited in part the tight timeline elections officials face as they continue processing and counting ballots. Attorneys for Peltola’s campaign had sued state elections officials, seeking a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected and the reasons for the rejections. They said their intent was to ensure that all qualified voters have their ballots counted. But attorneys for the state said the information requested would violate voter privacy.

items.excerpt: - AP - Nov 12, 2026 - 1 hr ago The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are almost here. Here's what to expect and how to watch The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are here, live from Las Vegas. So, what should you expect? Producer Edgar Barrera is once again in the top spot with 10 nominations this year. He's followed by Karol G, Rosalía, Jorge Drexler and hip hop duo Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso. They have seven each. The ceremony, which will begin at 8 p.m. Eastern, is being held at Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena. Performers at this year’s bash include Karol G, Anitta, Banda Los Recoditos, Jorge Drexler, Silvana Estrada and 2026 Latin Grammy Person of the Year Daddy Yankee. He is the first Latin urbano artist to receive this accolade. The show will air live on Univision, UniMás, Galavisión and ViX. Rapper Yella Beezy convicted of hiring gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 on busy Dallas interstate DALLAS (AP) — A Dallas County jury has unanimously convicted rapper Yella Beezy of capital murder in a brazen daylight attack on rapper MO3 on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020. Jurors found that Yella Beezy hired the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3. Yella Beezy’s real name is Markies Conway, and MO3’s real name was Melvin Noble. The jury’s guilty verdict means the 35-year-old Conway will spend the rest of his life in prison without parole. Kewon White was found guilty in September of carrying out the fatal shooting and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Irma P. Hall, 'Soul Food' and 'The Ladykillers' actor who found fame at 60, dies at 91 Irma P. Hall, the beloved actress known for roles in “Soul Food” and “The Ladykillers,” has died at 91. Her family announced her passing Wednesday, though no cause was given. Hall was best known as Big Mama in “Soul Food,” a role that earned her an NAACP Image Award. She also received a Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize for her role in “The Ladykillers.” Hall's acting career began later in life after decades as a teacher. She was a dedicated member of her church and helped develop young artists. Her family remembers her as a woman of faith and a global teacher. The 'Hunger Games' are back, with an A-list cast and brutal origin story for Haymitch The “Hunger Games” franchise is back with “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” focusing on a young Haymitch Abernathy. Before becoming the mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Haymitch was a tribute from District 12. Director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson cast a then-19-year-old Joseph Zada as Haymitch. Zada impressed with his charisma and mischief, essential for the role. The film's production spanned five months across Spain and Germany. The series has a lasting cultural impact, with over 100 million books sold and $3.3 billion in box office revenue. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also return in the epilogue. Jordan Firstman has been a lot of things, but 'Club Kid' confirms he's a filmmaker NEW YORK (AP) — It’s taken some time but Jordan Firstman, with “Club Kid,” feels like he’s finally made it. Since its debut at the Cannes Film Festival, “Club Kid” has been a sensation. Now, he just needs to stay on his game. The film, which Firstman wrote, directed and stars in, draws from Firstman's own experiences with gay nightlife. His character is hard-partying, hard-drug user who's shocked to discover he has a 10-year-old son. After a bidding war, A24 picked it up for $17 million and is releasing the film in the heart of awards season. Firstman has been a provocative viral-video star, a TV series writer, an actor and more. But “Club Kid” confirms he's a filmmaker. Movie Review: James Gray delivers a milestone crime drama in ‘Paper Tiger’ Miles Teller and Adam Driver play brothers trying to work on a deal in 1986 New York in James Gray's “Paper Tiger.” Part crime drama, part family tragedy, the film also stars Scarlett Johansson as Teller's wife, Hester. All are trying to make a little more money in pursuit of their version of the American Dream. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr opines that “with an operatic grace and 35 mm grit, “Paper Tiger” shrewdly and authentically explores ideas about wealth, worth, the cost of family and price of wanting more.” Rated R, “Paper Tiger” opens in limited release Friday and expands nationwide Nov. 20. What goes in to making hit Netflix period drama 'The Empress'? Thousands of candles, wigs and extras German period drama “The Empress” has been a big hit outside of Europe. That's despite the show following the rise and reign of Empress Elisabeth of the Austrian empire. Star Devrim Lingnau Islamoğlu says she's even been recognized in Peru. And showrunner Katharina Eyssen says she's been contacted on social media from fans as far afield as Ukraine, Iran and Africa. Philip Froissant portrays Emperor Franz Joseph I and has messages from followers who have visited the real palaces where the couple lived after seeing the program. “The Empress” returns for the third and final season on Thursday. The 2027 Coachella lineup is here: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to headline INDIO, Calif. (AP) — The 2027 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival lineup is finally here. Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, and SZA will headline the event next April. Tame Impala, the musical project of Australian Kevin Parker, returns as a headliner after first topping the bill in 2019. SZA and Lipa have also performed at Coachella before. Daddy Yankee, set to be named artist of the year at the 2026 Latin Grammys, joins as a fourth headliner. The festival will feature Madonna, Phoebe Bridgers, and many more. Coachella returns to Indio, California, for two weekends in April 2027. Tickets go on sale Friday. ... Walliams and Brand were leading UK comics. Now they are part of a reckoning over sexual misconduct LONDON (AP) — A day after British actor-comedian Russell Brand was sent to prison for rape and sexual assault, allegations have surfaced against another leading comedian, David Walliams. The cases have sparked a wider reckoning about celebrity misconduct in the U.K. Walliams, a feted children's author and well-known TV personality, is facing allegations of using his fame to exploit young female fans. He had sought to block news organizations from publishing these claims, but a judge dismissed his bid. Walliams has not been charged, but the revelations have prompted questions about the media and entertainment industries' roles in enabling such behavior. Authorities are now urging stronger protections for women.
